Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:78: And the pious Rabbi Lapidot, peace be upon him, testified to my teacher, peace be upon him, that he saw in a dream the pious sage Rabbi Yehuda bar Shoshan, peace be upon him, after his death, here in the Upper Galilee, and saw that his face shone like the light of the sun, and every single hair of his beard shone like a torch; and he asked him for what he had merited this. He said to him: for the virtue of silence that he had, for in all his days he never spoke an idle word. Behold, that not study but practice is the essential thing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:79: And concerning the matter of the death of infants, they elaborate in the Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim, and the exposition is lengthy; see there. Behold, this distinction pertains to the matter of judgment and fear, and we have seen fit to include it in this Gate, in order to include fear within love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:80: Further, among the things that cause and arouse a person to love his Creator is when he considers what the Holy One, blessed be He, promised through the prophets and the words of the holy spirit concerning the good of the World to Come that He is destined to bequeath to the righteous. Isaiah the prophet said (Isaiah 4:5), "and the LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory shall be a canopy." And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, from page 209 to page 213), they elaborate at length on the matters of the Garden of Eden, and explain this verse there. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Bava Batra, chapter 5, page 75b), explain this verse, in these words: "and the LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies" - Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to make, for every single righteous person, seven canopies in the Garden of Eden, as it is said, "and the LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day," and so on, "for over all the glory shall be a canopy." Rabbi Yochanan said: this teaches that for every single righteous person, the Holy One, blessed be He, makes a canopy according to his honor. And why do I need smoke in the canopy? Rabbi Chanina the Great said: because each one's canopy is singed by the canopy of his fellow [out of envy at its greater glory] - woe to that shame, woe to that humiliation - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:81: Further, concerning the secret of this mentioned verse, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, beginning of page 219) - and this is the end of the discourse we copied in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2 - in these words: it is taught, after seven days, the body becomes as it was, and his soul enters its place - it enters the Cave of Machpelah, sees what it sees, and enters the place it enters, until it reaches the Garden of Eden, and encounters the cherubim and the flame of the sword that is at the lower Garden of Eden; if it is righteous, it may enter, it enters. It is taught: four supports are ready, with one image of the body in their hands, and it clothes itself in it with joy and sits in that dwelling until the appointed time. Afterward, a herald calls out and a pillar of three colors is prepared, and that pillar is called "the habitation of Mount Zion," as it is written (Isaiah 4:5), "and the LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke, and the shining of a flaming fire" - it ascends through that pillar to the gate of "Tzedek" [Righteousness] of Zion, and Jerusalem is within it. If it merits to ascend further, its portion and lot are better, to cleave within the body of the King; and if it does not merit to ascend further, it is written (ibid. 4:3), "and it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy." And if it merits to ascend further, happy is it, for it has merited the honor of the King and to delight in the supernal delight above, from the place called "Shamayim" [Heaven], as it is written (Isaiah 58:14), "then you shall delight yourself in the LORD" - "in the LORD" precisely; happy is the portion of one who merits Chesed, as it is written (Psalms 57:11), "for Your kindness is great, reaching to the heavens" - is it only to the heavens? But is it not written (Psalms 108:5), "for Your kindness is great above the heavens"? Rabbi Yosi said: there is chesed and there is chesed - supernal Chesed and lower Chesed; supernal Chesed is above the heavens, lower Chesed is what is written (Isaiah 55:3), "the sure kindnesses of David" - and of these it is written "reaching to the heavens" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:82: Further, concerning the virtue of the Garden of Eden, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Chayei Sarah, pages 129-130), in these words: come and see, one who sanctifies himself and guards himself in this world so as not to be defiled, his dwelling in that world is among those supernal holy ones who perform their mission continually, and these stand in "the courtyard," as it is said, "the courtyard of the Tabernacle." And there are others who are further within, who are not in the courtyard but in the house itself, as it is said (Psalms 65:5), "we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house" - David said, "we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house" - since he already said "he shall dwell in Your courtyards," why does it say "we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house"? It should have said "he shall be satisfied with goodness," as it is written "he shall dwell" - rather, we have learned, there is no dwelling in the [Temple] courtyard except for the kings of the house of David alone, and there is a place for the supernal pious ones who enter within - and who are they? As it is written, "and those who camped before the Tabernacle, eastward, before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and his sons." And how many compartments upon compartments, and lights upon lights, are distinguished in that world, and each one is ashamed [outshone] by the light of its fellow - just as deeds are distinguished in this world, so too places and lights are distinguished in that world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:83: And concerning the virtues of the righteous in the Garden of Eden, they elaborate in the Yalkut, part 1 (Parashat Bereshit, section 20, page 6c), on the verse (Genesis 2:8), "and the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, to the east"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:84: And further, they say, of blessed memory, in the Sifrei (see Devarim, section 10), on the verse (Psalms 16:11), "fullness of joys [sova semachot]" - do not read "sova semachot" but "sheva semachot" [seven joys] - the faces of the righteous are destined, in the future to come, to be like the sun, the moon, the firmament, the stars, the lightning, the roses, the menorah of the Temple, and so on. And they bring a verse there for each and every one - and so too in the Midrash, Vayikra Rabbah, this discourse is brought on the verse "and you shall take for yourselves"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:85: And when he considers the goodness of the World to Come, how wondrous and hidden its matter is, of which it is said (Isaiah 64:3), "the eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for one who waits for Him" - it is fitting that he improve his deeds and love his Creator, since from the side of His great kindness He will give him a portion of that supernal pleasantness, as explained in the discourse, that from the side of Chesed it flows. And so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 36:8), "how precious is Your kindness, O God! And the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings. They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of Your house, and You shall give them to drink of the river of Your delights" - and they explain in the Tikkunim (page 88a) the secret of "the river of Your delights"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:86: And in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat "Shor O Chesev O Ez" (27:1), our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say, on this verse: Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Menachem said, it is not written "adnecha" [your Eden, singular] here but "adaneicha" [your Edens, plural] - this teaches that every single righteous person has his own Eden.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:87: And it says at the end of the discourse, "let not the foot of pride come against me" - for anyone who has within him an aspect of the entry of pride, like the foot that enters and exits, let him not come there, along the lines of (Proverbs 16:5), "everyone who is proud of heart is an abomination to the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:88: And although the pleasantness that the righteous merit comes from the side of Chesed, nevertheless the side of judgment accompanies this - that they examine with the utmost precision whether he is fit for that level or not, as it says in the discourse, "if he merits... and if he does not merit..." - and this is what is said (Psalms 36:11), "continue Your kindness to those who know You" - specifically.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:89: And so too he says (Psalms 31:20), "how great is Your goodness, which You have stored up for those who fear You, which You have wrought for those who take refuge in You" - they explain in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (7a), that "which You have wrought for those who take refuge in You" is said concerning the Garden of Eden, where the righteous stand in a garment resembling this world; see there. And "how great is Your goodness" is the secret of the light that the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the first day, which Moses used, and which He has stored away for the righteous in the future to come, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:90: And when a person wishes to discern the goodness of the World to Come through the matters of this world, he should see what is said in the wedding canopy of Elijah: three things are a glimpse of the World to Come - Shabbat, the sun, and marital relations - to this point. The explanation is that on Shabbat, the light revealed to us is a glimpse of the World to Come, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Bereshit Rabbah 11:2): the light of a person's face on Shabbat is not like [his face] on the weekdays. And so they say in tractate Shabbat (119a), concerning that gentile who asked why our Sabbath stew smells so good - they told him, we have a spice, and Shabbat is its name, and whoever does not observe Shabbat, his stew does not have that smell. And on the Shabbat day, from the side of the extra soul that comes, one feels a wondrous delight in his soul, and if he is wise, through it the secrets of the Torah are revealed to him - as I have seen this with my own eyes in my teacher, peace be upon him, and sages like him. And we have further elaborated on the matter of Shabbat being a glimpse of the World to Come in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 2; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:91: And likewise the sun is a glimpse of the hidden light - for just as no person can gaze at it when it is at its full strength, so no person can withstand the secret of the hidden light in this world; and in the future to come, it will be revealed to the souls in the lower Garden of Eden, "the sun of righteousness, with healing in its wings," as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 211a) - and we copied this discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 13. And so, in the future, it is said of the sun (Isaiah 30:26), "and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:92: And marital relations, that physical pleasure, is one-sixtieth of the pleasure of the World to Come; and in tractate Berachot (57b) they say that this pleasure is only the pleasure of the [lowest] orifices [i.e., a mere shadow of true pleasure].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:93: And a glimpse of the discernment of the pleasure of the World to Come is the matter of good fragrance, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains concerning the fragrance we smell at the conclusion of Shabbat; he says (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 208b): come and see, fragrance is the sustenance of the soul, because it enters the soul and not the body - "and he smelled the smell of his garments"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:94: And let us return to the exposition of the verse we were engaged in, concerning "He will do for one who waits for Him." Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 130b): come and see, happy are the righteous, for how much good is stored away for them for that world, and there is no inner place among all those like those who know the secret of their Master and know how to cleave to Him every day; of these it is written (Isaiah 64:3), "the eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for one who waits for Him." What is "for one who waits for Him" [lamechakeh lo]? Along the lines of (Job 32:4), "he waited [chikah] for Job with words" - and these are those who press toward the matter of wisdom, and are precise and wait for it, to know the clarity of the matter and to recognize their Master - these are the ones their Master praises every day; these are the ones who enter among the supernal holy ones, and these enter through all the gates above, and there is none who holds back their hands - happy is their portion in this world and the World to Come - to this point. And when you examine this whole matter, [you will see that] they are those who debate in divine wisdom to know the secret of the matter in its proper configuration, as explained at the beginning of the discourse, and so it says further on as well, "to know the clarity of the matter and to recognize their Master."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:95: And therefore a person must improve his deeds and always fear lest sin cause him not to be fit for that supernal level - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Berachot, first chapter, page 4a), that King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 27:13), "had I not believed to see the goodness of the LORD," and so on - they say, of blessed memory, it is taught in the name of Rabbi Yosi: why is there a dot over "lulei" [had I not]? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am assured of You that You pay a good reward to the righteous in the future to come, but I do not know whether I have a portion among them or not - to this point. And it says further on that he feared lest sin cause [his downfall]; and if King David, peace be upon him, was afraid and not confident in his deeds, what should one full of countless sins say, and on what should he rely, if not that he repent with complete repentance until the day of his death - and even so, perhaps.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:96: And one who is confident that he will merit the goodness of the World to Come without the intermediary of deeds is a fool and simpleton - for one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, what will he eat on Shabbat? For this is excluded - according to how a person toils, so he eats; and the goodness of the World to Come is not attained except through great alacrity and diligence. And to this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 13:4), "the soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing; but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat" - the explanation being that one who desires to delight in the World to Come with that taste, but does not perform the deeds fitting to attain that light, is "the soul of the sluggard," along the lines of their saying, that if he did not toil, what will he eat? And "the soul of the diligent," who are diligent in the occupation of Torah and commandments, "shall be made fat" in the World to Come, with supernal delight - for according to what he did, so he shall eat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:97: And although he toils, he should not rely on his deeds, but rather on the supernal Chesed that the Holy One, blessed be He, will grant him - as brought in Chovot HaLevavot, Gate of Trust (chapter 4), in these words: one of the pious used to say, a person does not attain the reward of the World to Come through his deeds if they are examined precisely in the reckoning of what he owes God for His goodness toward him, but rather through the kindness of God toward him - therefore do not trust in your deeds. And David said of this (Psalms 62:13), "and to You, O LORD, belongs kindness, for You repay a man according to his work" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:98: And he further writes there concerning the manner of trust in the World to Come, in these words: and the proper manner of trust in God is that one occupy himself with the causes that bring him to the fitting levels of the pious - namely, that he conduct himself with the attributes of the ascetics who despise this world, removing his love and choice from his heart and exchanging it for love of Him, blessed be He, giving himself over to Him and delighting in Him, and being astonished at the world and its inhabitants, and conducting himself in the customs of the prophets and the pious, with his heart trusting in God that He will deal kindly with him as He dealt kindly with them in the World to Come. But one who trusts that God will grant him this without the intermediary of deeds is a fool and a simpleton, comparable to those of whom it is said, they perform the deed of Zimri and seek the reward of Pinchas.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:99: And among the signs of people of this great virtue is that the servants of the Creator acknowledge [the value of] the service of the Creator, and endurance at the time of trial and distress - that every matter becomes light in their eyes compared to the fulfillment of the commandment of the Creator, blessed be He - as you know from "and God tested Abraham," and the matter of Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya in the fiery furnace, and Daniel in the lions' den, and the Ten Martyrs of the government, and whoever chose death in the service of the Creator over life in rebellion against Him, and poverty over wealth, and illness over health, and distress over peace, and gave himself over to the judgment of the Creator and desired His decree - such a one is fit for the kindness of the Creator toward him, in the pleasantness of the World to Come, of which Scripture says (Proverbs 8:21), "to cause those who love me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:100: And along these lines, to the strictness with which my teacher, peace be upon him, treated the acquisition of the goodness of the World to Come, they are strict in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 4a) concerning [proper conduct/qualities] - in the incident of Rabbi Chiya, when he saw Rabbi Shimon, of blessed memory: meanwhile he saw several great, supernal wings, and Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Elazar his son ascended upon them and rose to the academy of the firmament, and all these wings were waiting for them. He saw that they were being restored and renewed in their splendor and light, greater than the light of the splendor of the sun. Rabbi Shimon opened and said: let Rabbi Chiya enter and see how the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to renew the faces of the righteous for the time to come. Happy is he who enters here without shame, and happy is he who stands in that world like a mighty pillar in everything - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:101: And further on: a voice returned as before and said: supernal, hidden, concealed ones, with open eyes, who roam through the whole world - look and see the lower ones sleeping, sealed in their holes - awaken! Who among you turns darkness to light and tastes bitter as sweet, before you come here? Who among you waits every day for the light that shines at the time the King commands the doe [i.e., dawn] and the King is honored above all the kings of the world? Whoever does not anticipate this every day in that world has no portion here - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:102: And what it says, "happy is he who enters here without shame" - shame can occur in one of two ways: the first, that he have no shame entering the King's Heichal because of his evil deeds - for this is the shame that troubles people, as it says, "let us lie down in our shame, and let our confusion cover us, for we have sinned against the LORD our God" (Jeremiah 3:25) - will he not be ashamed and humiliated when they see the ledgers of his evil deeds before all the pious and righteous in the Garden of Eden, as we copied incidents of judgment in the Garden of Eden in the Gate of Fear, chapter 13; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:103: The second, shame may also reach him if he did not occupy himself with Torah properly - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, Second Heichal, page 247b), in these words: this holy Chayah stands when the soul ascends and reaches it, and then it asks the soul concerning the secret of the wisdom of its Master, and according to that wisdom that it pursued and cleaved to, so they give it reward; and if it was able to cleave but did not cleave, it is pushed outside and does not enter, and stands beneath that Heichal in shame. And when those seraphim beneath it lift their wings, they all strike with their wings and burn it, and it is burned and yet not burned, standing and yet not standing - and so it is judged every day, shining and not shining; and even though it has good deeds, because it has no reward in that world like those who strive in wisdom to gaze upon the honor of their Master - and there is no measure to the reward of those who know wisdom in the honor of their Master - happy is their portion in this world and the World to Come, as it is written (Proverbs 3:13), "happy is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who obtains understanding" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:104: And what it says, "happy is he who stands in that world like a mighty pillar in everything" - the intent is that he was strong in divine service, like a strong pillar that does not totter, so that if he began performing some service, such as the matter of rising early for synagogue or rising at midnight, he does not abandon the service under any circumstances in the world, but binds an oath upon his soul to fulfill that commandment - as King David, peace be upon him, says in the psalm (Psalms 15:1), "who shall sojourn in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain?" - and he says that one of the attributes is, "he swears to his own hurt, and does not change" - and the Radak and the other commentators explain that the explanation of "swears to his own hurt" is to harm his own body through fasting and mourning from pleasures, and likewise to diminish his purse for charity and commandments and the like, and does not change what he swore, even though it harms his body - and this is along the lines of what David says (Psalms 119:106), "I have sworn, and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous ordinances."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:105: And along these lines is also (Avot 3:13), "vows are a fence for abstinence" - in general, to be firm. And so too in the Tikkunim (page 21a), concerning the matter of whoever fixes a place for his prayer - for according to how the souls act, so the Shechinah rests with them: a soul that is fixed in prayer or in Torah is a place for the Shechinah to rest in it, but a soul that has no fixed practice in prayer or Torah, but only happens upon it by chance, so the Shechinah rests upon it by chance - and this is "as when a bird's nest chances before you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:106: Further, "mighty" also means that he should not be overcome by his evil inclination even in the slightest matters - for if he is overcome in one thing, he will be overcome in another, and separate from divine service. And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot compares (Gate of Abstinence, chapter 5) the matters of service and abstinence to a strand of crystal beads joined by a thread - if you loosen one bead from it, they will all scatter and their joining will be ruined; and he says, therefore strive to be careful with all of them, and then you will have help for the rest, as they say, of blessed memory (Avot 4:2), that one commandment leads to another commandment; and the sage says, concerning the succession of good things one after another (Proverbs 8:34), "happy is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my gates" - and he says first "listens," and afterward "to watch," and afterward "to guard" - to this point. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, says in brief, "like a mighty pillar in everything" - meaning, in all the commandments and matters of service that a person can fulfill in all of them, he must be strong, not to be overcome.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:107: It further says, "with open eyes, who roam through the whole world" - my teacher, peace be upon him, explains that these are the seven eyes of the LORD that roam through the whole earth in the world to watch over the deeds of people, as we elaborated in the Gate of Fear. "Look and see" - that they watch below - and here the matter breaks off.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:108: And it further says, "the lower ones sleeping" - meaning, the lower people, who sleep the sleep of blindness - awaken to the service of the Creator! "Who among you turns darkness to light" - meaning, to turn judgment into mercy - and this is when a person overcomes his inclination, for the evil inclination is drawn from the left and the good inclination from the right, and when the evil inclination is subdued beneath the good inclination, the left is included in the right, and darkness turns to light and bitter to sweet. And there is one who explains that it means to turn the measure of night, which is darkness, into light, through the occupation with Torah, which is called light - and this is correct.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:109: "Who among you waits every day for the light," and so on - my teacher, peace be upon him, explains that this is a warning to those who rise from midnight onward to occupy themselves with Torah, that they not return to sleep, but rather must stay awake and wait for the light that shines, and so on - namely, at the "darkness of dawn," as explained in Parashat Beshalach (46a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:110: Behold, it is explained how many things a person must do to merit that supernal pleasantness, and their essence is rising at midnight to recite Torah until day, as it says, "whoever does not anticipate this every day has no portion here." And this attribute he mentions at the end of the matter, because rising at midnight is not possible while one has evil deeds, for the attributes require correspondence with one another - and therefore he must first have repentance and [good] deeds, in order to overcome his inclination and the other matters, along with the attribute of rising early to recite Torah. Up to here have arrived the general points that a person must discern in order to love his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:111: And when you consider all the aforementioned contemplations, you will find that they are all from the side of Chesed - whether in the creation of the world, as it says (Psalms 89:3), "I have said, the world is built with kindness"; whether in the creation of man through a holy soul; whether in the matter of sustenance from the side of Chesed, as it says (ibid. 136:25), "who gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever"; whether in the matter of death, of which it is said "very good," for the reason we explained; whether in his reward in the World to Come, "and to You, O LORD, belongs kindness" (ibid. 62:13), and likewise (ibid. 57:11), "for Your kindness is great above the heavens," as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:112: And the rest of the particulars are all from the side of Chesed - such as the matter of the four who must give thanks, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Berachot, page 54b), in these words: Rav Yehuda said, four must give thanks - those who go down to the sea, those who travel through deserts, one who was ill and recovered, and one who was imprisoned in jail - and of all of them it is written, "let them give thanks to the LORD for His kindness." And the place where Chesed is revealed more than all of them is in one who was ill and recovered, for he reaches the gates of death - as Elihu explains concerning the sick person (Job 33:20-23), "and his soul makes his life abhor bread, and his soul dainty food; his flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen," and so on, "and his soul draws near to the pit," and so on, "if there be for him an angel, an intercessor, one out of a thousand, to show man his uprightness; then He is gracious to him, and says, deliver him from going down to the pit" - and they explain, of blessed memory (Shabbat, page 32a), that even if nine hundred and ninety-nine accuse him and one advocates in his favor, he is saved; see there. This certainly indicates the complete kindness toward His creatures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:113: And when a person discerns all the kindnesses the Holy One, blessed be He, has done for him specifically, from the day he came into the air of the world until he stood as a grown man, they cannot be told for their abundance - such that he is obligated to serve the Creator with complete love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:114: Further, among the aspects of Chesed is that He, blessed be He, accepts man in repentance after he has sinned, as it says, "His right hand is outstretched to receive the penitent" - and this is that Chesed spreads even to the husk, to raise the soul from there. And this matter is revealed in the Torah (Leviticus 14:3), "and the priest shall go out of the camp to purify the leper" - and even in Gehinnom (Psalms 139:10), "even there Your hand shall lead me, and Your right hand shall hold me" - and this is "Your hand shall lead me" - the hand of judgment - "shall lead me" there, in Gehinnom, for the cleansing of the soul; "and Your right hand shall hold me" - to raise it from there - and this is "His right hand is outstretched." I heard the root of this idea from my teacher, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:115: And several other particulars the author of Chovot HaLevavot elaborates (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3), concerning God's kindnesses to man - whether in his creation from nothing into being, or in the perfection of his limbs, all of them complete, or in the completion of his intellect and the like - for all this is supernal kindness, even though he is obligated by the strict law, from the side of his sins. And even one who lacks one of his limbs should accept his sufferings out of love, as will be further explained, that one is obligated to accept sufferings out of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:1: This chapter will explain the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel. It says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 25), of blessed memory: "I am the LORD your God" (Exodus 20:2) - blessed be the Omnipresent, who chose Israel from among all the nations, from all who come into the world, and from all the works of His hands, and acquired them as a complete acquisition, as children and as servants, and called them by His name - many times He speaks with them, and when He speaks with them, He speaks with them in love, for He loved them with the joy He rejoiced in them. Therefore a person is obligated to say, when will my deeds reach the deeds of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who acquired this world and the World to Come and the days of the Messiah only through good deeds and the study of Torah? Therefore a person is obligated to say, for my sake the world was created. With what does a person acquire [merit with] his Father in Heaven? Through deeds and the study of Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, grants him as an acquisition this world, the days of the Messiah, and the World to Come. A person acquires [merit with] his Father in Heaven through love, through brotherhood, through friendship, through truth, through peace, through much sitting [in study], through little business, through the give-and-take of Torah, through attending upon the Sages, through the give-and-take of the Gemara, through lowliness of spirit, through humility, through "no, no" [refusing falsehood], and through "yes, yes" [affirming truth].
